data.critique: Clean Aurora call. Strong dose-dependent increases in cell_area (z to +10.5) and nuc_area (z to +6.0) with falling cell_count (z to −7.0) occur in all 4 wells, and the microscopist independently notes occasional bi- and tri-nucleated cells with intact tubulin and actin networks — behaviour characteristic of chromosome segregation/cytokinesis failure in polyploid cells. Runner-ups are not materially supported: DNA replication appears only as 1/10 neighbour in the initial 2-well comparison and drops to 0/10 in the final 4-well comparison; Eg5 inhibition would typically raise the mitotic-like fraction (not observed: z −0.72 at the highest dose); and microtubule stabilizers would produce spindle/bundling defects not seen in the bundles-free microtubule images. The modest absolute neighbour similarity (~0.37 mean) and the microscopist's own 'Moderate' uncertainty appropriately temper confidence, so 0.80 is not overconfident. Minor caveat: proportions reported by morphology proxies are inconsistent, but the direct visual observations dominate that noisy proxy and are direction-consistent for Aurora kinase inhibition.

reflection.text:
The Aurora call was driven by coherent morphology: massive cell enlargement (cell_area z=+9.6 to +10.5), nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z=+6.0, nuc_major_axis z=+4.1), cell loss (cell_count z=-7.0), and microscopist observation of lower density with bi- and tri-nucleated cells with intact tubulin/actin. The atlas comparison was unanimous 4/4 wells and 10/10 neighbours as Aurora kinase inhibitors, so the 0.80 probability seemed justified.
What misled me was phenotypic convergence: cisplatin-induced DNA damage can produce enlarged, multinucleated polyploid-like cells that mimic chromosome segregation/cytokinesis failure. I over-weighted the unanimous vote and under-weighted its weakness - mean similarity only ~0.37, range 0.276-0.423 - and dismissed the early 1/10 DNA replication neighbour signal. Dose-response trends (cell_area rho=+0.80 p=0.2, nuc_area rho=+0.20 p=0.8, cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6) were direction-consistent but non-significant and should have tempered confidence.
Acquisition choices locked in the error: I sampled only 0.1, 1, 3, 10 uM with morphology and cell/nuclear size features plus a single describe_phenotype visual, and my post-unblinding searches for cisplatin polyploidy/enlargement returned 0 hits. Without a DNA-damage vs mitosis discriminator I had no way to break the Aurora vs DNA-damage degeneracy.
what_was_right: Detected strong dose-associated cell and nuclear enlargement with cell loss: cell_area z=+9.6 at 1 uM and +10.5 at 10 uM, nuc_area z=+6.0 at 1 uM and +5.8 at 3 uM, cell_count z=-7.0 at 10 uM.
Flagged polyploidy-like morphology with low solidity, altered eccentricity/roundness and microscopist-noted bi-/tri-nucleated cells and lower density.
Noted low absolute neighbour similarity (~0.37 mean) and Moderate microscopist uncertainty, correctly signaling less than certain evidence.
what_was_wrong: Attributed enlarged multinucleated phenotype solely to Aurora kinase inhibition, missing that cisplatin DNA inhibitor activity (CID 5702198, ChEMBL DNA target) can produce the same enlargement/polyploidy mimic.
Over-relied on unanimous NSC 4/4 and 10/10 neighbour vote in e8 despite low similarities 0.276-0.423, and discarded the early DNA replication 1/10 signal in e4.

Treated non-significant dose-response correlations in e9-e11 (p=0.2-0.8, n=4 wells) as supportive without testing DNA-damage markers or mitotic fraction that would separate Eg5/Aurora from DNA damage.

## Conclusion

**Aurora kinase inhibitors** (stated probability 0.80); key evidence e8, e5, e3, e2, e7.

Why: Unanimous NSC 4/4 and 10/10 neighbours plus enlarged bi/multinucleate cells support this class.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: DNA-content flow cytometry plus phospho-histone H3 immunofluorescence to quantify polyploidy and mitotic defects, comparing to a reference of the leading class.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean Aurora call. Strong dose-dependent increases in cell_area (z to +10.5) and nuc_area (z to +6.0) with falling cell_count (z to −7.0) occur in all 4 wells, and the microscopist independently notes occasional bi- and tri-nucleated cells with intact tubulin and actin networks — behaviour characteristic of chromosome segregation/cytokinesis failure in polyploid cells. Nearest-neighbour comparison is unanimous 4/4 with 10/10 top neighbours annotated as this class. Runner-ups are not materially supported: DNA replication appears only as 1/10 neighbour in the initial 2-well comparison and drops to 0/10 in the final 4-well comparison; Eg5 inhibition would typically raise the mitotic-like fraction (not observed: z −0.72 at the highest dose); and microtubule stabilizers would produce spindle/bundling defects not seen in the bundles-free microtubule images. The modest absolute neighbour similarity (~0.37 mean) and the microscopist's own 'Moderate' uncertainty appropriately temper confidence, so 0.80 is not overconfident. Minor caveat: proportions reported by morphology proxies are inconsistent, but the direct visual observations dominate that noisy proxy and are direction-consistent for Aurora kinase inhibition.

## Unblinding

Compound: **cisplatin** (PubChem CID [5702198](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5702198))

Identity check: mismatch: name gives CID 5702198, BBBC021 structure gives CID 2767 (Cantide + Cisplatin)

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The Aurora call was driven by coherent morphology: massive cell enlargement (cell_area z=+9.6 to +10.5), nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z=+6.0, nuc_major_axis z=+4.1), cell loss (cell_count z=-7.0), and microscopist observation of lower density with bi- and tri-nucleated cells with intact tubulin/actin. The atlas comparison was unanimous 4/4 wells and 10/10 neighbours as Aurora kinase inhibitors, so the 0.80 probability seemed justified.
What misled me was phenotypic convergence: cisplatin-induced DNA damage can produce enlarged, multinucleated polyploid-like cells that mimic chromosome segregation/cytokinesis failure. I over-weighted the unanimous vote and under-weighted its weakness - mean similarity only ~0.37, range 0.276-0.423 - and dismissed the early 1/10 DNA replication neighbour signal. Dose-response trends (cell_area rho=+0.80 p=0.2, nuc_area rho=+0.20 p=0.8, cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6) were direction-consistent but non-significant and should have tempered confidence.
Acquisition choices locked in the error: I sampled only 0.1, 1, 3, 10 uM with morphology and cell/nuclear size features plus a single describe_phenotype visual, and my post-unblinding searches for cisplatin polyploidy/enlargement returned 0 hits. Without a DNA-damage vs mitosis discriminator I had no way to break the Aurora vs DNA-damage degeneracy.

What was right:
- Detected strong dose-associated cell and nuclear enlargement with cell loss: cell_area z=+9.6 at 1 uM and +10.5 at 10 uM, nuc_area z=+6.0 at 1 uM and +5.8 at 3 uM, cell_count z=-7.0 at 10 uM.
- Flagged polyploidy-like morphology with low solidity, altered eccentricity/roundness and microscopist-noted bi-/tri-nucleated cells and lower density.
- Noted low absolute neighbour similarity (~0.37 mean) and Moderate microscopist uncertainty, correctly signaling less than certain evidence.

What was wrong or missed:
- Attributed enlarged multinucleated phenotype solely to Aurora kinase inhibition, missing that cisplatin DNA inhibitor activity (CID 5702198, ChEMBL DNA target) can produce the same enlargement/polyploidy mimic.
- Over-relied on unanimous NSC 4/4 and 10/10 neighbour vote in e8 despite low similarities 0.276-0.423, and discarded the early DNA replication 1/10 signal in e4.
- Treated non-significant dose-response correlations in e9-e11 (p=0.2-0.8, n=4 wells) as supportive without testing DNA-damage markers or mitotic fraction that would separate Eg5/Aurora from DNA damage.

Proposed next experiment: Run DNA-content flow cytometry plus gamma-H2AX vs phospho-histone H3 (Ser10) / phospho-Aurora immunofluorescence for cisplatin alongside a bona fide Aurora inhibitor and DMSO control to distinguish DNA damage-induced enlarged multinucleated polyploid cells from direct Aurora inhibition.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [25058905](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25058905/): Cisplatin in cancer therapy: molecular mechanisms of action. *Eur J Pharmacol* (2014) — Cisplatin acts through formation of DNA lesions that activate DNA damage response pathways.
- PMID [36368406](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36368406/): Cisplatin in cancer treatment. *Biochem Pharmacol* (2022) — Cisplatin anti-cancer activity is attributed to DNA damage mechanisms.
- PMID [38520407](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38520407/): APLF facilitates interstrand DNA crosslink repair and replication fork protection to confer cisplatin resistance. *Nucleic Acids Res* (2024) — Cisplatin sensitivity is governed by interstrand DNA crosslink repair and replication fork protection.
